artifact_kind: concrete fixture freeze; satisfies the predecessor's implementation_entry_gate. NO implementation, NO result claimed.
what_this_freezes: The exact candidate identities, accepted quality vectors, held-constant physical facts and expected decision of every world, before any witness code exists. The predecessor said: 'Freeze the concrete fixture, numeric inputs, exact expected preference changes and cost-authority path before implementation.' This is that freeze.
the_claim_restated_narrowly: Same search state, same candidates, same policy, same physical facts; change ONLY accepted observation values -> the measured-candidate preference changes, through the frontier machinery that already exists in `decision.rs`. Nothing is added to the comparator.

stages_in_order: 1. promotion class: `ranking_score.class.tier()`; max tier forms the pool; tier 0 => None{EveryMoveWorthless}

2. proxy ordering: the non-dominated frontier via `SearchCandidate::proxy_dominates` (no worse on every comparable proxy, strictly better on at least one). frontier.len()==1 => SelectForAuthority{decided_by_physical_gain:false}
4. frontier>1 and any comparable difference => Ambiguous{ConflictingOrderingProxies} -- explicitly NOT scalarised
5. frontier>1, proxies all Equal => physical tie-break on `ranking_score.gpu_ms_saved`; unique best => SelectForAuthority{decided_by_physical_gain:true}
the_machinery_being_exercised.why_this_is_the_right_target: It is already ordinal-only and already refuses to trade one proxy against another. PARETO-1 does not need a new ranking rule -- the predecessor's out_of_scope forbids one -- it needs to prove accepted VALUES reach this comparator and move its answer.

the_quality_knob.helper: `state::fixtures::authority_reading(kl_p99: f64, route_flips: u64)` -> QualityBank, wrapped by `ingest::tests::Fixture::observed(kl)`
the_quality_knob.why_it_suffices: It exposes exactly TWO independently settable dimensions that both order, which is the minimum needed to build both agreement (dominance) and conflict (no dominance) without touching production code.
the_quality_knob.what_Fixture_observed_nulls: `routing.route_weight_mass_moved`, `top10_mass_displaced`, `top1_mass_displaced` are set to None, so RouteMixtureMass*, Top10MassDisplacedP99 and Top1MassDisplaced are UNOBSERVED and are excluded by `comparable()`. This is a property of the fixture, not of the model.
the_quality_knob.constant_and_therefore_inert: `positions` = 8 and `min_covered_mass` = 0.6315 are identical on every candidate in every world. Statistic::Positions and Statistic::CoveredMass therefore compare Equal, which neither breaks dominance nor supplies it.
the_quality_knob.direction: Statistic::better() -- KlP99, Top1Flips, Top10Changes, RouteFlips, RouteFlipRate are Better::Lower; Positions and CoveredMass are Better::Higher. Lower kl and fewer route flips are BETTER.

candidates.source: The fixture's `ActionVocabulary` already enumerates exactly two MapEdits -- `compile-all` (layers 0..0, all projections) and `compile-q` (layers 0..0, q_proj). LOOP-1's witness asserts `initial.census().enumerated == 2`.
candidates.identity_rule: The two candidate KEYS are whatever `CandidateSet` assigns from those edits. They MUST be read from the enumerated set at implementation time and pinned into the test as constants -- never guessed from the edit names, and never depended on positionally. R4-F1 is the standing reminder that input order must not reach a decision.

held_constant_across_every_world: the initial authoritative SearchSnapshot (serialised once, deserialised per world)
the candidate set and both candidate state keys
the observed-key SET (both worlds observe the same two keys; only the VALUES differ)
the gate and the search policy
the physical cost facts -- `ranking_score.gpu_ms_saved` IDENTICAL on A and B in W1/W2/C1 (see physical_facts_are_deliberately_inert)
`ParticipationDeclaration` on both candidates, so no dimension is excluded on one side only (R4-F10)

worlds.expected_evidence: `dominated` == [B]; `deciding` names BOTH ordering statistics that separated them (kl p99 and the route-flip statistic(s) that order); `decided_by_physical_gain` == false
worlds.why: A is no worse on every comparable proxy and strictly better on at least one, so the frontier has exactly one member and stage 2 returns.

worlds.purpose: the SAME machinery selects B when only the accepted values swap
worlds.expected_evidence: `dominated` == [A]; `deciding` the same statistic set as W1; `decided_by_physical_gain` == false
worlds.why: This is the whole claim. W1 and W2 differ in NOTHING except the accepted quality values, and the preferred candidate changes. `decided_by_physical_gain == false` in both is what proves the change came from quality rather than from economics.

worlds.purpose: conflicting proxies must refuse rather than manufacture a winner
worlds.expected_decision: Ambiguous{ candidates: [A, B] sorted, reason: ConflictingOrderingProxies }
worlds.why: A is better on kl, B is better on route flips, so neither dominates and the frontier keeps both. There is no calibration licensing a trade between kl places and routing places, so the refusal IS the correct answer. A winner here would be the defect.

worlds.purpose: the physical control the predecessor requires -- indistinguishable quality, separated by grounded cost
worlds.physical: gpu_ms_saved DIFFERS between A and B; the better value is preregistered before the run
worlds.expected_decision: SelectForAuthority{ candidate: the preregistered better-gain candidate } with `decided_by_physical_gain` == true and `deciding` EMPTY
worlds.why: Every comparable proxy is Equal, so stage 5 is reached and physical evidence legitimately separates them. The empty `deciding` plus the true flag is what distinguishes this from W1/W2 in the trace -- a reader never has to guess which stage decided.

worlds.purpose: identity must never break a tie
worlds.physical: gpu_ms_saved IDENTICAL on A and B
worlds.expected_decision: Ambiguous{ candidates: [A, B] sorted, reason: IndistinguishableOnEveryProxy }
worlds.why: Nothing separates them on any axis the search is allowed to use. `decide_promotion` is not given identity, so it cannot fall back on it. Naming a winner here would resurrect R4-F1.

worlds.accepted: W1's values, then a second admission carrying a substituted/incomplete run report
worlds.expected_decision: the ingestion refuses; the preference and every persisted fact are byte-identical to W1's
worlds.why: Inherited from LOOP-1/OPT-6 rather than reinvented; restated here because PARETO-1 must show a REJECTED observation cannot move preference either, not only that an ACCEPTED one can.

assertions_beyond_the_verdict: W1 and W2 produce DIFFERENT preferred candidates while their observed-key sets are equal as sets -- assert the key sets explicitly, or the result is the LOOP-1 claim again wearing a new name.
`decided_by_physical_gain == false` in W1 and W2, and `true` in C2. Without this, a physical tie-break could be reported as value-sensitivity.
Reopen each resulting snapshot and re-derive: the same preference and the same deciding evidence come back.

Permute the enumeration order of the candidate set in every world; the decision and the RECORD (`dominated`, `deciding`, both sorted) are unchanged. This re-arms the R4-F1 guard at the PARETO-1 layer.
No unregistered weighted quality-cost scalar appears anywhere in the witness -- the predecessor forbids one by name.

preconditions_to_verify_before_writing_t.note: Each of these can invalidate the fixture above. They are checks, not assumptions, and the fixture is re-pinned if any fails.
preconditions_to_verify_before_writing_t.P1_both_candidates_share_a_tier: If `ranking_score.class.tier()` differs between A and B, stage 1 filters one out and the frontier is NEVER exercised -- quality would then have no say and the witness would pass for the wrong reason. Confirm both land in the same tier under every world's values, W1 and W2 included.
preconditions_to_verify_before_writing_t.P2_at_least_two_statistics_actually_orde: `comparable()` requires `observed.is_some()` AND `evidence(registry, policy).orders()` AND both participations. Confirm by direct inspection that kl p99 AND at least one route-flip statistic pass all three under this fixture's registry and policy. If the route-flip family is Unusable at diagnostic scale, C1 is unconstructible and a different second dimension must be found before anything is implemented.
preconditions_to_verify_before_writing_t.P3_the_route_flip_pair_moves_together: RouteFlips and RouteFlipRate both derive from `routing.route_flips` over a constant `positions`, so they agree by construction. That is fine -- they are one dimension wearing two names, and the freeze treats them as one. They must never be counted as two independent agreeing proxies in any narrative of the result.
preconditions_to_verify_before_writing_t.P4_physical_facts_are_genuinely_inert_in: Assert `gpu_ms_saved` equality on A and B in those three worlds. If it differs, stage 5 could decide C1 and the refusal would be spurious.

physical_facts_are_deliberately_inert.what: W1, W2 and C1 hold `gpu_ms_saved` EQUAL across candidates. C2 is the only world where it differs, and there quality is equal.
physical_facts_are_deliberately_inert.why: It separates the two questions cleanly. PARETO-1 answers 'do accepted observation values reach the comparator and move it'. It does not answer 'is the physical number trustworthy'. Letting both vary at once would make a passing witness unable to say which one did the work.

the_realization_cost_gap_recorded_not_fi.finding: `represent::execution_cost::predict` models decode time as `gpu = baseline_gpu_ms_per_token * (1.0 - beta * wanted)`, where `beta = gpu fraction removed / byte fraction removed`. The calibration observation is chosen by filtering on `model_identity` and then taking the nearest `byte_fraction_removed`. CODEC IS NOT A KEY, and REALIZATION IS NOT A KEY.
the_realization_cost_gap_recorded_not_fi.consequence: For one model there is one beta and the form is monotone: more bytes removed always predicts less GPU time.
the_realization_cost_gap_recorded_not_fi.the_contradicting_measurement: PR #420, direct K-quant execution vs widening on the same model: U4 direct 2.0x FASTER, U6 1.8x SLOWER, U8 2.8x SLOWER, while streamed bytes fell 97.4 GB -> 25.9 / 20.0 / 13.7 per position. U8-direct is beta < 0 where the calibrated beta is ~0.79. The current parameterisation cannot hold both signs for one model, so this is not an unmeasured case -- it is an INEXPRESSIBLE one.
the_realization_cost_gap_recorded_not_fi.where_it_would_bite: Stage 5 of `decide_promotion` -- the `decided_by_physical_gain` path -- reads `ranking_score.gpu_ms_saved`, which descends from this model.
the_realization_cost_gap_recorded_not_fi.why_it_is_NOT_fixed_here: The predecessor's out_of_scope bars a lowering-vocabulary redesign, and its implementation_entry_gate says to RECORD a missing boundary rather than change production semantics inside this result. PARETO-1 holds physical facts constant in exactly the worlds where the defect could matter (see physical_facts_are_deliberately_inert), so its claim does not depend on beta being right.
the_realization_cost_gap_recorded_not_fi.what_it_becomes: A separate follow-on contract: realization-qualified execution cost, with #420's U4/U6/U8 arms as its first calibration set -- three codecs, one model, one of them with the opposite sign. The module already anticipates the axis and misses it: `CalibrationStatus::Provisional` and `DISTINCT_BREADTH_MIN_SEPARATION` guard beta against varying with BREADTH, while the module doc says a curve should later be learned 'across breadths and codecs'. Codec is in the aspiration and absent from the lookup.
the_realization_cost_gap_recorded_not_fi.sequencing_reason: Once PARETO-1 has passed, the beta work is no longer entangled with 'does the optimiser loop work at all', which makes it a much stronger transition to run on its own.

not_an_acceptance: A world in which the observed-key SET differs -- that is LOOP-1's AlreadyObserved result, not this one.
A preference change explained by `decided_by_physical_gain == true`.
A display-order or `display_order()` result described as a scientific preference.
SelectForAuthority described as a completed promotion or an installed incumbent.
Any world whose candidates sat in different tiers, where stage 1 and not the frontier did the work.
out_of_scope_unchanged: No K3 download or run, no kernel work, no lowering-vocabulary redesign, no new unmeasured-candidate ranking rule, no change to `decide_promotion` itself.
